notes: Descriptions and requirement lines are verbatim from the books. 'requirements' is the structured form the rules layer checks; every entry must hold for the talent to be available.

Designer decision: the pool is the Core General talents, the six department lists, and the species talents for the prototype's species (Andorian, Human, Tellarite, Trill, Vulcan from Core; Caitian from the Species Sourcebook). Augment/Cybernetic and Esoteric talents are left out.
Designer decision: species talents are species-only (the book's 'or gamemaster's permission' is not offered); a mixed-heritage character counts as both parent species.

Designer decision: Untapped Potential and Veteran follow the book's Step Five: Novice receives Untapped Potential, Veteran receives Veteran, Experienced chooses freely. Their score/rank caps are kept as 'limits' data and are not enforced yet.
Designer decision: 'era' is present on every talent for later filtering; null means available in every era. Nothing is filtered yet.
Prototype: the player character is always a main character. Role requirements are checked against the Captain's Log assignment (the same senior-staff posts the book calls roles).
Prototype: Personal Effects is selectable once; the book's per-item repeats need an item choice the prototype does not have yet.
Prototype: Psychoanalyst's 'psychology-related focus' is matched by a focus name containing 'psych'. Fellowship Specialty's focus is chosen from the character's own focuses.

Effects are structured descriptions for later systems; no talent effect is applied to gameplay yet. Types: reroll, freeDie, difficulty, ignoreDifficultyIncrease, bonusMomentum, groupMomentum, threatCost, maxStress, protection, impact, ignoreResistance, substitute, obtainInformation, complication, focus, value, trait, attack, determination, special.

careerLengthTalents.note: Core p.127–128 Step Five: Novice and Veteran each receive a single fixed talent; Experienced chooses freely.

omitted.name: Constant Presence
omitted.reason: Supporting character only; the player character is a main character.

omitted.name: Aenar, Bajoran, Betazoid, Cardassian, Denobulan, Ferengi, Klingon, Orion and Romulan talents
omitted.reason: Species not in the prototype's species list.

talents.name: Back-Up Plans
talents.description: Whenever you or an ally fail a task (so long as you are present in the scene), you may add 1 point to the group’s Momentum pool.

effects.when: you or a present ally fail a task

talents.name: Bold
talents.description: Choose a department when you select this talent. Whenever you attempt a task from that department, and you buy one or more d20s by adding Threat, you may re-roll a single d20. You may select this talent multiple times, once for each department. You may not select this talent for any department for which you have the Cautious talent.

effects.when: task with the chosen department after buying d20s with Threat

talents.name: Calm and Logical
talents.description: When you gain a trait which represents a mood or emotional state, you may suppress that trait (ignoring its effect) for the duration of a single task or a single turn in combat by suffering 1 Stress.

effects.when: you gain a mood or emotional-state trait

talents.name: Cautious
talents.description: Choose a department when you select this talent. Whenever you attempt a task with that department, and you buy one or more d20s by spending Momentum, you may re-roll a single d20. You may select this talent multiple times, once for each department. You may not select this talent for any department for which you have the Bold talent.

effects.when: task with the chosen department after buying d20s with Momentum

talents.name: Close-Knit Crew
talents.description: When a scene begins, if there are fewer points of Momentum in the group pool than there are characters in the scene who have this talent, immediately add 1 Momentum to the group pool.

effects.when: scene begins with less Momentum than characters present with this talent

talents.name: Collaboration
talents.description: Choose a single department when you select this talent. Whenever an ally attempts a task using that department, you may spend 1 Momentum (Immediate) to allow them to use your rating for that department and one of your relevant focuses.

effects.when: an ally attempts a task with the chosen department

talents.name: Constantly Watching
talents.description: At the start of an action scene, the gamemaster must spend an additional 2 Threat to have an NPC take the first turn. You may also re-roll 1d20 on any task attempted to locate a hidden enemy or danger.

effects.when: an NPC takes the first turn of an action scene
task to locate a hidden enemy or danger

talents.name: Dauntless
talents.description: Whenever another character attempts to intimidate or threaten you, you may suffer 2 Stress to ignore their attempt.

effects.when: another character attempts to intimidate or threaten you

talents.name: Extra Effort
talents.description: When you attempt a task, you may reduce the Difficulty of the task by 1, to a minimum of 0. However, once the task is completed, you immediately take Stress equal to the original Difficulty of the task.

effects.when: any task

talents.name: Indefatigable
talents.description: When you fail a task, and attempt that task again during the same scene, reduce the Difficulty of the second attempt (and any subsequent attempts if you still fail) by 1.

effects.when: retrying a failed task in the same scene

talents.name: Gut Feeling
talents.description: When the gamemaster spends Threat to introduce reinforcements or to cause a Reversal, they must spend 2 additional Threat to do so. This is 2 extra Threat in total, not per reinforcement.

effects.when: the gamemaster introduces reinforcements or causes a Reversal

talents.name: Methodical Planning
talents.description: When an ally attempts a task which benefits from a trait you created which represents your plan or strategy, then you may Assist that ally’s task even if you are not present. In combat, this assistance does not require you to use your task to Assist that ally.

effects.when: an ally’s task benefits from your plan or strategy trait

talents.name: No Hesitation
talents.description: At the start of any round in an action scene, you may add 1 Threat to take the first turn, regardless of who would otherwise have acted first.

effects.when: start of a round in an action scene

talents.name: No Pain, No Gain
talents.description: When you fail a task (but not an opposed task) which used your Daring, you may always choose to Succeed at Cost.

effects.when: you fail a non-opposed Daring task

talents.name: Personal Effects
talents.description: You possess some significant and uncommon item or device which is not standard issue, but which is nevertheless useful for missions. You may select this talent multiple times, gaining a different item each time.

effects.when: always

talents.name: Quick Survey
talents.description: At the start of a scene, you may immediately ask one question, as if you had spent 1 Momentum on the Obtain Information Momentum Spend. The answer can only provide information that you could obtain with your own senses: you cannot gain information from equipment in such a short time.

effects.when: start of a scene (own senses only)

talents.name: Reassuring
talents.description: When you succeed at a task using your Presence, you may spend Momentum to reassure your allies, so long as they are able to hear you. You may spend 1 Momentum (Repeatable) to allow one ally who can see and hear you to recover 1 Stress. That ally may not recover more than 3 Stress from one use of this talent.

effects.when: you succeed at a Presence task

talents.name: Second Wind
talents.description: You may spend Determination at the start of your turn to remove the Defeated state, and to recover up to half of your maximum Stress. The normal requirements for spending a point of Determination still apply.

effects.when: start of your turn

talents.name: Self-Reliant
talents.description: Whenever you succeed at a task where you did not purchase additional dice by spending Momentum or adding to Threat, you generate bonus Momentum equal to the task’s Difficulty. Bonus Momentum cannot be saved.

effects.when: you succeed without buying extra dice

talents.name: Studious
talents.description: Whenever you spend 1 or more Momentum to Obtain Information, you may ask one additional question (in total, not per Momentum spent on Obtain Information).

effects.when: you spend Momentum to Obtain Information

talents.name: Technical Expertise
talents.description: Whenever you attempt a task assisted by the ship’s Computers or Sensors, you may re-roll one d20 in your pool, or you may allow the ship to re-roll its d20.

effects.when: task assisted by the ship’s Computers or Sensors

talents.name: Tough
talents.description: Your maximum Stress is increased by 2.

talents.name: Voice of Authority
talents.description: When you Assist someone, and use your Presence to do so, you may add 2 Threat to treat your assistance die as if it had rolled a 1 instead of rolling it.

effects.when: you Assist using Presence

talents.name: Well-Informed
talents.description: You have contacts everywhere and you listen to news and rumors from far and wide. At the start of a scene, you may add 1 Threat to ask the gamemaster two questions about the situation or location, as if you had spent Momentum on the Obtain Information spend. The answers you receive will be knowledge you’ve gained from your contacts and the news and rumors you’ve heard.

effects.when: start of a scene

talents.name: Proud and Honorable
talents.description: Whenever you attempt a task to resist being coerced into breaking a promise, betraying your allies, or otherwise acting dishonorably, you may add Threat to immediately succeed at the task. The amount of Threat you add is equal to the task’s Difficulty.

effects.when: resisting coercion to act dishonorably

talents.name: The Ushaan
talents.description: You are experienced in the tradition of honor-dueling known as the Ushaan. When you make a Melee Attack, or are targeted by a Melee Attack, and buy one or more d20s by adding to Threat, you may re-roll any number of dice in your dice pool for the task. Further, you own an Ushaan-tor, a razor-sharp ice-miner’s tool used in these duels. The Ushaan-tor is a blade (see page 242), and it counts as standard issue for you.

effects.when: Melee Attack made or received, after buying d20s with Threat

talents.name: Resolute
talents.description: Your Maximum Stress increases by an amount equal to your Command rating.

talents.name: Spirit of Discovery
talents.description: You have an additional option you may pick when you spend Determination: you may immediately add 3 Momentum to the group pool.

talents.name: Incisive Scrutiny
talents.description: When you succeed at a task using Control or Insight, you may ask one question, as if you had spent Momentum to Obtain Information.

effects.when: you succeed at a Control or Insight task

talents.name: Asking the Right Questions
talents.description: When you attempt a task that relates to information you’ve received from Obtain Information questions in the current scene, you may re-roll 1d20.

effects.when: task related to Obtain Information answers this scene

talents.name: Joined
talents.description: You are bonded with a symbiont and have lifetimes of memories to draw upon. You gain an additional character trait, which is the name of the symbiont; this reflects potential advantages of being Joined, as well as the ability to perform rites and rituals to awaken past hosts’ memories, and the vulnerabilities inherent in the connection. Furthermore, up to twice per adventure, you may declare that a past Host had experience or expertise in a particular field: you gain an additional focus when you do this, which remains for the rest of the adventure.

effects.when: you declare a past host’s expertise

talents.name: Former Initiate
talents.description: You joined the Initiate Program, hoping to be chosen by the Symbiosis Commission to become Joined. As there are far more Initiates than there are symbionts, you were one of many who failed, but the capabilities of even a failed Initiate are highly sought after by Starfleet and other organizations. When you attempt a task using Control or Reason, and you spend Determination to set a die as a 1, you may also re-roll your dice pool after the roll. You cannot select this talent if you have the Joined talent.

effects.when: Control or Reason task after spending Determination to set a die to 1

talents.name: Kolinahr
talents.description: You have undergone the ritual journey to purge all emotion, allowing you to dispassionately observe and dissect your emotional responses and render them powerless. When you ignore emotions using your Mental Discipline Species Ability, you may avoid emotional traits by taking 1 Stress instead of 2, and you no longer increase the potency of emotional traits when Fatigued.

effects.when: ignoring emotions with Mental Discipline

talents.name: Mind Meld
talents.description: You’ve undergone training in telepathic techniques that allow the melding of minds through physical contact. This always requires a task (normally Control + Sciences) with a Difficulty of at least 1, which can be opposed by an unwilling participant. If successful, you link minds with the participant, sharing thoughts and memories. Momentum may be spent to gain more information or perform deeper telepathic exchanges. This link goes both ways, and it is a tiring and potentially hazardous process. Complications can result in taking Stress, pain, disorientation, or lingering emotional or behavioral difficulties.

talents.name: Nerve Pinch
talents.description: You have learned numerous techniques for the stimulation and control of nerve impulses—collectively called neuropressure. Some applications of neuropressure can be used to incapacitate assailants swiftly and non-lethally. The nerve pinch counts as a Melee Attack which inflicts Stun Injuries with a Severity of 3 and the Intense quality. You may use Science or Medicine instead of Security when attempting a Nerve Pinch Attack.

effects.when: Nerve Pinch Attack

talents.name: Disarming Nature
talents.description: Some Caitians are extremely social beings, adept at putting others at ease. Whenever you attempt a task to make another creature relax or trust you, you may reduce the Difficulty by 1. If this is part of an extended task, your Impact is increased by 1.

effects.when: task to make another creature relax or trust you
the same task as part of an extended task

talents.name: Feral Aggression
talents.description: Some Caitians tend towards a territorial manner, reacting to threats with anger, and pain with defiance. You gain 1 Protection, and whenever you suffer a trait that represents pain or fear, you may add 1 Threat to remove that trait immediately.

effects.when: you suffer a pain or fear trait

talents.name: Advanced Team Dynamics
talents.requirementText: Command 4+, main character only, commanding officer or executive officer only
talents.description: The first time you introduce a supporting character in a mission, that supporting character may take one additional option to improve the supporting character (from the list on page 146).

effects.when: first supporting character introduced in a mission

talents.name: Advisor
talents.description: Whenever you Assist another character using your Command, the assisted character may re-roll one d20.

effects.when: you Assist using Command

talents.name: Bargain
talents.description: When you use Negotiation to make an offer to someone during social conflict, you may re-roll a single d20 on your next Persuade task to convince that person. If the social conflict with that person involves an extended task, your Impact is increased by 1.

effects.when: next Persuade task after a Negotiation offer
that social conflict is an extended task

talents.name: Bolster
talents.description: When you succeed at any task using your Command during an action scene, you may spend Momentum to recover Stress suffered by your allies. When you spend 1 Momentum (Repeatable), one ally who can see and hear you recovers 1 Stress. You may affect multiple allies, but each ally affected may only recover 1 Stress in this way each time this talent is used.

effects.when: you succeed at a Command task in an action scene

talents.name: Call Out Targets
talents.description: When you Assist a character in an Attack, the assisted character generates 2 bonus Momentum if their Attack succeeds. Bonus Momentum cannot be saved.

effects.when: an Attack you Assist succeeds

talents.name: Call to Action
talents.description: In a conflict, you may use the Prepare minor action to grant one ally who you can communicate with a minor action of their choice, which they perform immediately.

effects.when: Prepare minor action in a conflict

talents.name: Cold Reading
talents.description: When you succeed at a task during social conflict, you generate 1 bonus Momentum which must be used for the Obtain Information Momentum spend to gain knowledge about one of the people you’re interacting with. If the social conflict with that person involves an extended task, you may ignore any Resistance the extended task has.

effects.when: you succeed at a task during social conflict
social-conflict extended task

talents.name: Coordinated Efforts
talents.description: When you Assist another character during an extended task, the character you Assist increases their Impact by 1.

effects.when: you Assist during an extended task

talents.name: Decisive Leadership
talents.description: In a conflict, once per round, you or your allies may Keep the Initiative for free.

effects.when: in a conflict

talents.name: Defuse the Tension
talents.description: Whenever you attempt a task to persuade someone not to resort to violence, the first d20 you purchase for that task is free.

effects.when: task to persuade someone not to resort to violence

talents.name: Follow My Lead
talents.description: When you succeed at a task during combat or another perilous situation, you may spend Determination. If you do, choose a single ally who can hear you. The next task that ally attempts counts as having assistance from you, using your Presence + Command. On this task, do not roll your assistance die: it counts as having already rolled a 1.

effects.when: you succeed during combat or peril

talents.name: Multi-Discipline
talents.description: You may select one additional Role Benefit, which may not be Commanding Officer.

talents.name: Plan of Action
talents.description: Whenever an ally succeeds at a task that was made possible, or had a reduced Difficulty, because of a trait you created, and that trait represented a plan, strategy, or course of action, they generate 2 bonus Momentum. Bonus Momentum cannot be saved.

effects.when: an ally succeeds thanks to your plan trait

talents.name: Precautions
talents.description: Once per scene, when an ally suffers an Injury or the ship suffers a Breach, prevent that Injury or Breach; describe what precaution you took to prevent the issue.

talents.name: Supervisor
talents.description: The ship’s Crew Support increases by 1. This increase is cumulative if multiple main characters select it.

talents.name: Teacher
talents.description: When you create a trait for an ally that represents your guidance or advice, that ally may re-roll one d20 on a single task they attempt which benefits from that trait.

effects.when: a task that benefits from your guidance trait

talents.name: Attack Run
talents.description: Whenever you take the Attack Pattern major action, enemy Attacks against you do not reduce in Difficulty due to that action.

effects.when: Attack Pattern major action

talents.name: Covering Advance
talents.description: When you succeed at a task to maneuver your ship, you may spend 2 Momentum to provide cover for allied ships. When an enemy vessel next makes an Attack, before the beginning of your next turn, if you are the closest ship to that attacker but they do not target you, the difficulty of their Attack is equal to your ship’s Scale.

effects.when: enemy attacks an ally ship while you are closest

talents.name: Efficient Evasion
talents.description: When you attempt an Evasive Action major action for the second or subsequent time in a row during a scene, you add 1 Momentum to the group pool.

effects.when: repeated Evasive Action in a row

talents.name: Fly-By
talents.description: Whenever you use the Swift Action Momentum spend, you do not increase the Difficulty of the second task if one of the tasks you attempt is to pilot a vessel.

effects.when: Swift Action where one task is piloting

talents.name: Glancing Impact
talents.description: Whenever you succeed at the Evasive Action major action, increase the Resistance of the ship you are piloting by 2; this bonus lasts until the start of your next turn.

effects.when: successful Evasive Action

talents.name: Hands-on Pilot
talents.description: When you perform the Warp, Evasive Action, or Attack Pattern major actions, the ship may count its focus range as double the relevant department rating (i.e., if the ship has a Conn of 3, it will score a critical success on any roll of 6 or less). However, when anyone else pilots the ship, increase the complication range by 1.

effects.when: Warp, Evasive Action, or Attack Pattern

talents.name: Inertia
talents.description: When you use the Impulse minor action, you may spend 1 Momentum to move one additional zone so long as you used the Impulse minor action or Warp major action in your previous turn.

effects.when: Impulse after Impulse or Warp last turn

talents.name: Multi-tasking
talents.description: When you attempt the Override major action while at a bridge station that includes one or both helm or navigator positions, you may use your Conn department instead of the department usually required for that task.

effects.when: Override from a helm or navigator station

talents.name: Pathfinder
talents.description: Whenever you attempt a task to plot a course through unknown territory, reduce the Difficulty of the task by 1, 2, or 3, to a minimum of 1. For each point by which you reduce the Difficulty, increase the complication range of that task.

effects.when: plotting a course through unknown territory

talents.name: Precise Evasion
talents.description: Whenever you use the Evasive Action major action, the ship does not suffer the increased Difficulty for Attacks normally caused by Evasive Action.

effects.when: ship Attacks after Evasive Action

talents.name: Precision Maneuvering
talents.description: Whenever you attempt a task that requires precise or careful maneuvering, or where there is a risk of colliding with another object, you may re-roll 1d20.

effects.when: precise maneuvering or collision risk

talents.name: Push the Limits
talents.description: When you attempt a Conn task that has increased in Difficulty due to environmental conditions or damage to the engines, you may add 1 Threat to ignore the difficulty increase.

effects.when: Conn task hampered by environment or engine damage

talents.name: Spacewalk
talents.description: Whenever the Difficulty of a task would be increased due to low- or zero-gravity, ignore that Difficulty increase. If a task that was normally possible would be made impossible because of low- or zero-gravity, you may attempt the task at +1 Difficulty instead.

effects.when: low or zero gravity

talents.name: Starship Expert
talents.description: Whenever you take a Conn task to identify a type of starship, or to try to understand an unknown form of starship, you gain 1 bonus Momentum, which may only be used on the Obtain Information Momentum spend, or to pay part of the cost of the Create Trait Momentum spend (where the trait must represent some form of known or observed weakness in the ship being studied).

effects.when: Conn task to identify or understand a starship

talents.name: Strafing Run
talents.description: Whenever you take the Attack Pattern task and then Keep the Initiative, the cost to Keep the Initiative is reduced to 0. If the character taking the next turn makes an Attack, they may re-roll one d20.

effects.when: after Attack Pattern
their Attack after your Attack Pattern

talents.name: Thread the Needle
talents.description: When you perform the Impulse minor action or Warp major action when piloting a starship, enemy Attacks from ships with a greater Scale than yours increase in difficulty by +1. If attacked by a ship with a Scale that is double or more the Scale of your ship, then you increase the Difficulty by 2 instead.

effects.when: larger ships attack after your Impulse or Warp (+2 if double Scale)

talents.name: Visit Every Star
talents.description: You gain an additional focus, and one of your focuses (either the one gained from this talent, or an existing one) must relate to Astronavigation, Stellar Cartography, or a similar field of space science. Further, when you succeed at a navigation-related task, you gain 1 bonus Momentum due to your knowledge and familiarity. Bonus Momentum cannot be saved.

effects.when: you succeed at a navigation task

talents.name: Zero-G Combat
talents.description: In combat, when you make an Attack while in a zero-gravity or micro-gravity environment, you may use the higher of your Conn or Security departments for the task, and you ignore any difficulty increases caused by the lack of gravity. In addition, enemies who lack similar training increase the Difficulty of Attacks against you by 1.

effects.when: Attack in zero or micro gravity
untrained enemies attack you in zero gravity

talents.name: I Know My Ship
talents.description: Whenever you attempt a task to determine the source of a technical problem with your ship, the first bonus d20 you purchase is free.

effects.when: finding the source of a technical problem with your ship

talents.name: I’m Giving It All She’s Got!
talents.description: Once per scene, when the ship has no Reserve Power remaining at the start of your turn, you may add 2 Threat to gain Reserve Power.

talents.name: In the Nick of Time
talents.description: Whenever you succeed at an Engineering or Science task as part of an extended task, you increase your Impact by 1.

effects.when: Engineering or Science task in an extended task

talents.name: Jury-Rig
talents.description: Whenever you attempt an Engineering task to perform repairs, you may reduce the Difficulty by 2, to a minimum of 0. If you do this, however, then the repairs are only temporary and will last only a single scene before they fail again; you may increase this duration by one scene by spending 1 Momentum (Repeatable). Jury-rigged repairs can only be applied once, and the Difficulty to repair a device that has been Jury-rigged increases by 1.

effects.when: Engineering repair task (temporary repairs)

talents.name: Maintenance Specialist
talents.description: You may ignore the first complication rolled on any Engineering task. Further, when you create any equipment trait, any character who uses that piece of equipment in a task may ignore the first complication rolled.

effects.when: any Engineering task, or using your equipment trait

talents.name: Meticulous
talents.description: During a timed challenge or extended task, before rolling, you may take one die and treat it as if it had already rolled a 1, but if you do, the task will take one additional interval.

effects.when: timed challenge or extended task

talents.name: Miracle Worker
talents.description: Whenever you succeed at an Engineering task to overcome an extended task, you may increase your Impact by 1 by spending 1 Momentum instead of 2.

effects.when: Engineering task in an extended task

talents.name: More Power!
talents.description: Whenever you use the Reroute Power major action, you may spend 2 Momentum to give Reserve Power to two systems, rather than one.

effects.when: Reroute Power

talents.name: Past the Redline
talents.description: When you use advanced technology, including attempting a task assisted by the ship, you may choose to increase the complication range by 1, 2, or 3. If you succeed, then you gain bonus Momentum equal to the amount by which the complication range was increased. Bonus Momentum cannot be saved.

effects.when: using advanced technology

talents.name: Percussive Maintenance
talents.description: When you attempt a Control + Engineering task, you may add 1 Threat to use your Daring instead of your Control. If you do this, and the task succeeds, then you may reduce the time taken by 1 interval without spending Momentum.

effects.when: Control + Engineering task

talents.name: Procedural Compliance
talents.description: When you attempt an Engineering task, you may remove one d20 from your dice pool before rolling. If you do so, you gain one automatic success on your task.

effects.when: Engineering task

talents.name: Repair Team Leader
talents.description: You are trained to direct and lead damage repair teams during emergencies, giving them your guidance and expert knowledge of the ship’s systems. If you succeed at the Damage Control major action (page 303) you may spend 2 Momentum (Repeatable) to repair one additional Breach.

effects.when: successful Damage Control

talents.name: Right Tool for the Right Job
talents.description: Whenever you acquire an engineering tool with an Opportunity Cost, that equipment trait of that tool gains +1 Potency (typically this will result in Potency 2). If the tool is used in an extended task, whoever is using that tool increases their Impact by 1.

effects.when: acquiring an engineering tool with an Opportunity Cost
that tool is used in an extended task

talents.name: Saboteur
talents.description: When you make an Attack against a structure, machine, or stationary vehicle while in personal combat (i.e., you aren’t using a ship’s weapons to make the Attack), you may use your Engineering instead of your Security to resolve the Attack.

effects.when: personal Attack against a structure, machine, or stationary vehicle

talents.name: Transporter Chief
talents.description: You’re well-versed in the operation of transporter systems and can often get them to function in extreme circumstances or to achieve outcomes that few could manage. Such efforts are never without risk, given the delicacy of the technology. When you attempt a task to use, repair, or modify a transporter, you may add 2 Threat to reduce the Difficulty of the task by 2, to a minimum of 0.

effects.when: using, repairing, or modifying a transporter

talents.name: Ambush Tactics
talents.description: When you succeed at an Attack against an enemy who is unaware of your presence, or who is suffering from a trait or complication which represents a weakness or vulnerability, increase the Severity of the Attack by 2.

effects.when: target unaware or suffering a weakness trait

talents.name: Applied Force
talents.description: When you make a Melee Attack, you may use Fitness instead of Daring. In addition, you add 1 to the Severity of your Unarmed Attacks.

effects.when: Melee Attack
Unarmed Attack

talents.name: Close Protection
talents.description: When you make a successful Attack, you may spend 1 Momentum to protect a single ally within Close range. The next Attack against that ally before the start of your next turn increases in Difficulty by 1.

effects.when: next Attack against a protected ally

talents.name: Crisis Management
talents.description: The Momentum cost to use the Direct major action (page 289) is removed.

talents.name: Defensive Training
talents.description: Select either Melee Attacks or Ranged Attacks when you acquire this talent. Attacks against you of the chosen type increase in Difficulty by 1.

effects.when: Attacks of the chosen type against you

talents.name: Fire at Will
talents.description: If you make an Attack, you may use the Swift Action Momentum spend for 1 Momentum rather than 2, but the second major action you take must also be an Attack.

effects.when: both major actions are Attacks

talents.name: Get Down!
talents.description: You and any allies within Close range gain +1 Protection while in Cover.

effects.when: in Cover

talents.name: Interrogation
talents.description: When you succeed at a task to coerce someone to reveal information in a social conflict, you may ask one question for free, as per the Obtain Information Momentum spend.

effects.when: successful coercion for information in social conflict

talents.name: Lead Investigator
talents.description: Whenever you attempt a task to retrieve or analyze evidence of a crime, you may re-roll 1d20. When you spend one or more Momentum to Obtain Information to ask questions about a crime scene or evidence, you may ask one additional question.

effects.when: retrieving or analyzing evidence of a crime
Obtain Information about a crime scene or evidence

talents.name: Martial Artist
talents.description: Your Unarmed Strike Attack may be used to inflict Deadly Injuries as well as Stun Injuries.

talents.name: Mean Right Hook
talents.description: Your Unarmed Strike Attack gains the Intense quality.

talents.name: Pack Tactics
talents.description: Whenever you Assist another character during combat, the character you assisted gains 1 bonus Momentum if they succeed.

effects.when: you Assist during combat

talents.name: Piercing Salvo
talents.description: When you make a Torpedo Attack, you may spend 2 Momentum (Immediate) to add the Piercing quality.

effects.when: Torpedo Attack

talents.name: Precision Targeting
talents.description: You can more easily pick out and target specific systems when making an Attack against an enemy vessel. When you make an Attack with starship weapons that targets a specific ship system, you may re-roll a d20.

effects.when: starship Attack targeting a specific system

talents.name: Quick to Action
talents.description: During the first round of any combat, you and your allies may ignore the normal cost to Keep the Initiative.

effects.when: first round of combat

talents.name: Steady Hands
talents.description: When you take the Aim minor action (page 288) before a Ranged Attack, you add 1 to the Attack’s Severity, in addition to the other effects of aiming.

effects.when: Ranged Attack after Aim

talents.name: Applied Research
talents.description: Once per scene, when you attempt a task which relates to information you received earlier that scene from an Obtain Information question, the first bonus die you purchase is free.

effects.when: task related to Obtain Information answers this scene

talents.name: Baffling Briefing
talents.description: When you engage in a social conflict using deception, you may use Science in place of Command so long as their technical knowledge is used to mislead their opponent.

effects.when: deception in social conflict using technical knowledge

talents.name: Computer Expertise
talents.description: Whenever you attempt a task that involves the programming or study of a computer system, the first bonus d20 you purchase is free.

effects.when: programming or studying a computer system

talents.name: Dedicated Focus
talents.description: When this talent is taken, choose one of your focuses. When attempting a task where that focus applies, you score a critical success for any die which rolls equal to or under twice the relevant department.

effects.when: task where the chosen focus applies

talents.name: Did the Reading
talents.description: When you attempt a task, you may spend 1 Momentum (Immediate) to use Science on that task instead of the department you would normally use. In addition, you count as having an applicable focus for that task. Each time after the first in a single scene that you use this ability, the Momentum cost increases by 1: this is cumulative.

effects.when: any task

talents.name: Expedition Expert
talents.description: Prior to participating in an away team mission, you may make additional preparations by spending 2 Momentum (Immediate). During the expedition, any member of the away team may re-roll a single d20 on any task to navigate the terrain or circumvent a hazard or obstacle. The away team may re-roll a total number of dice in this way equal to your Science rating.

effects.when: navigating terrain or circumventing hazards on an away mission

talents.name: Intense Scrutiny
talents.description: Whenever you succeed at a task using Reason or Control as part of an extended task, you ignore any Resistance on that extended task.

effects.when: Reason or Control task in an extended task

talents.name: Lab Rat
talents.description: When attempting an extended task while using a laboratory, increase your Impact by 1.

effects.when: extended task in a laboratory

talents.name: Learn from Failure
talents.description: When you fail at a Science task, you may add 3 Threat to create a trait which represents knowledge or insights gained from the failure. The cost of this is reduced by 1 for each success you scored on the failed task.

effects.when: you fail a Science task

talents.name: Mental Repository
talents.description: Using extensive mental conditioning, you have access to memories with unprecedented clarity and accuracy. You may treat Obtain Information as if it were an Immediate Momentum spend, but the answers to these questions can only come from information you would already know and remember.

effects.when: answers from your own memory

talents.name: Rapid Analysis
talents.description: When you succeed at a Science task, the cost of the Reduce Time Momentum option is reduced to 1.

effects.when: successful Science task

talents.name: Rapid Hypothesis
talents.description: Once per scene, when you ask two or more questions using Obtain Information, you may immediately create a trait representing your theoretical understanding of the subject of those questions.

effects.when: asking two or more Obtain Information questions

talents.name: Student of War
talents.description: You have conducted extensive research into numerous kinds of conflict and has devoted your academic career to the study of war. While this knowledge may be purely theoretical, such information, when placed into the hands of more capable combatants, can be truly devastating. When you Assist a character making an Attack or taking the Guard action in combat, they may re-roll one d20.

effects.when: you Assist an Attack or Guard action

talents.name: Testing a Theory
talents.description: When you attempt a task using Engineering or Science, the first bonus d20 you purchase is free, so long as you succeeded at a previous task covering the same scientific or technological field earlier in the same adventure. If you created a trait that represents a hypothesis about an unknown phenomenon, you may also re-roll one d20 on tasks related to that hypothesis.

effects.when: Engineering or Science task in a field you succeeded at earlier this adventure
task related to your hypothesis trait

talents.name: Theory into Practice
talents.requirementText: Science 3+ and Testing a Theory talent
talents.description: When you succeed at a task using Engineering or Science where you gain the additional d20 from the Testing a Theory talent, or which benefits from a trait that represents a hypothesis you’ve made, you generate 2 bonus Momentum. Bonus Momentum may not be saved.

effects.when: Engineering or Science success using Testing a Theory or your hypothesis trait

talents.name: Walking Encyclopedia
talents.description: Once per session, when you attempt a task, you may spend 2 Momentum (Immediate) to gain an additional focus for the remainder of the session, due to your breadth of knowledge. However, any task using that focus increases its complication range by 1, as you are not a true expert on that subject.

effects.when: tasks using that focus

talents.name: Bedside Manner
talents.description: When you succeed at a Medicine task to heal an Injury, you may immediately remove a trait from the patient, even if that trait was unrelated to the Injury being treated. In addition, when you attempt a Reputation Check, add one additional positive influence.

effects.when: successful Medicine task to heal an Injury

talents.name: Chief of Staff
talents.description: When you Assist another character attempting a Medicine task, each assisting character may re-roll their assistance die.

effects.when: you Assist a Medicine task

talents.name: Combat Medic
talents.description: When attempting a Medicine task during combat, you may pick one trait which increases the Difficulty of the task and ignore it.

effects.when: Medicine task during combat

talents.name: Cutting Edge Medicine
talents.description: Whenever you attempt a Medicine task with a Difficulty of 3 or higher, you may spend up to 3 Momentum (Immediate) to reduce the Difficulty by the number of Momentum spent, to a minimum Difficulty of 1. However, as these latest advances are often experimental, the complication range of the task increases by 1 for each Momentum spent.

effects.when: Medicine task of Difficulty 3+

talents.name: Cyberneticist
talents.description: When you attempt a task to work on, install, or remove a cybernetic device from a patient, the first bonus d20 you purchase is free.

effects.when: working on, installing, or removing a patient’s cybernetic device

talents.name: Diagnostic Expertise
talents.description: When you succeed at a Medicine task to identify and diagnose the nature of a medical problem, you may ask one question—as per Obtain Information—for every additional d20 you bought by spending Momentum.

effects.when: successful diagnosis

talents.name: Doctor’s Orders
talents.description: When you attempt a task to coordinate others, or to coerce someone into taking or refraining from a specific course of action, you may use your Medicine department instead of Command.

effects.when: coordinating or coercing others

talents.name: Don’t You Die on Me!
talents.description: When a character is killed, you may spend Determination to make one attempt to revive them. If they were killed instantly by an Attack, then this may only be attempted within that scene. If the character suffered an Injury and died because they didn’t receive medical treatment in time, this may be attempted before the end of the subsequent scene. This requires a Daring + Medicine task, with a Difficulty of 3. If successful, the character is brought back from the brink of death, though they will remain Defeated for the remainder of the adventure. Failure means that your efforts were unsuccessful and the character dies.

effects.when: a character is killed

talents.name: Fellowship Specialty
talents.description: Select a focus. When you succeed at a Medicine task where that focus applies, the cost of the Create Trait Momentum spend is reduced to 1.

effects.when: successful Medicine task where the chosen focus applies

talents.name: Field Medicine
talents.description: When attempting a Medicine task, you may ignore any increase in Difficulty or complication range for working without the proper tools or equipment.

effects.when: Medicine task without proper tools

talents.name: First Response
talents.description: When you attempt the First Aid task during combat, the first die you purchase is free. Further, you may always Succeed at Cost, with each complication you suffer adding 1 to the Difficulty of healing the patient’s Injury subsequently.

effects.when: First Aid during combat
First Aid during combat

talents.name: Insightful Guidance
talents.description: Whenever you Assist a character in a social conflict, using your knowledge of psychology or emotional states, that character is considered to have a beneficial trait (Psychological Profile) in addition to the normal benefits provided by your Assist.

effects.name: Psychological Profile
effects.when: you Assist in a social conflict

talents.name: Positive Reinforcement
talents.requirementText: Ship’s Counselor role, Medicine 3+, and Presence 9+
talents.description: Once per mission, you may attempt a Presence + Medicine task with a Difficulty of 3, while providing emotional or mental treatment for another character. Success creates a character trait for your patient that lasts until the end of the mission: Boosted Confidence. In addition to the normal effects of the trait, that character can reroll their dice pool, as if they’d spent Determination, once before the end of the mission. If the task the character used their reroll on fails, they lose the trait created by this talent.

talents.name: Practice Makes Perfect
talents.description: After you have succeeded in a Medicine task, the Difficulty of any other Medicine tasks attempted that scene to treat or heal the same kind of Injury, poison, disease, or other ailment is reduced by 1.

effects.when: later Medicine tasks this scene for the same ailment

talents.name: Psychoanalyst
talents.description: When you use Medicine during a social conflict, you may increase the complication range of your task by 1, 2, or 3. For each step of complication range increased, you may ask a single question as if you’d spent Momentum on Obtain Information. Any Complications generated from this task results in the individual you are interacting with becoming offended or upset with being “analyzed.”

effects.when: Medicine during a social conflict

talents.name: Quick Study
talents.description: When attempting a task that will involve an unfamiliar practice, technique, or medical procedure, or which is to treat an unfamiliar species, ignore any Difficulty or complication range increase stemming from your unfamiliarity.

effects.when: unfamiliar practice, procedure, or species

talents.name: Stimulant Shot
talents.description: When you perform the First Aid task to revive a Defeated ally, you may add 1 Threat to let that ally recover Stress equal to your Medicine rating. A character may only benefit from this talent once per adventure.

effects.when: First Aid to revive a Defeated ally

talents.name: Surgery Savant
talents.description: When attempting a Medicine task during an extended task relating to surgery, your Impact is increased by 1. Impact is explained in more detail on page 271.

effects.when: Medicine task in a surgery extended task

talents.name: Triage
talents.description: When you attempt a task to identify specific Injuries or illnesses, or to determine the severity of a patient’s condition, you may spend 1 Momentum (Repeatable) to diagnose one additional patient.

effects.when: identifying Injuries or illnesses

talents.name: Untapped Potential
talents.description: Select one of your attributes when you receive this talent. You’re inexperienced, but talented and with a bright future. You may not have or increase any attribute to above 11, or any department to above 4 while you have this talent (and may have to adjust attributes and departments accordingly at the end of character creation). Whenever you succeed at a task for which you bought one or more additional dice (by any means), roll a d20 after the roll. If you roll equal to or less than the chosen attribute, gain 1 bonus Momentum; if you roll higher, add 1 Threat instead. While you possess this talent, you cannot gain any higher rank than Lieutenant (junior grade), or a higher enlisted rate than Petty Officer.

effects.when: you succeed after buying extra dice

talents.name: Veteran
talents.requirementText: Veteran (during character creation, or at gamemaster’s discretion)
talents.description: You’re wise and experienced, and draw upon inner reserves of willpower and determination in a measured and considered way. Whenever you spend Determination, roll a d20. If you roll equal to or less than your Control rating, you immediately regain that point of Determination. If you are Starfleet or military, you hold a rank of at least lieutenant commander, or an enlisted rate of at least chief petty officer.

effects.when: you spend Determination
